title: The righteous will be in delight.
subtitle: Where the record of the obedient leads

row.title: the obedient
sub: did not meet Him with sin

then: After the noble writers, the surah shows where the record leads. Ibn Kathir says the righteous are {idea}those who obeyed Allah and did not meet Him with disobedience.{/idea} {reward}Delight is what awaits them.{/reward}
now: You picture the righteous as people with perfect beards and perfect prayer streaks. {idea}The tafsir says the obedient.{/idea} Someone who keeps turning back to Allah after slipping is walking that road.
old: The righteous are a different kind of person from me.
new: The righteous are those who obey Allah, and I can be one of them.
try: Choose one act of obedience you find hard and do it once today, for Allah.

title: And the wicked will be in the Fire.
subtitle: The other end of the record
then: The verse sits directly opposite the one before it. Ibn Kathir says Allah {trap}mentions that the evildoers will be in Hell{/trap}, after naming the delight of the obedient. {idea}Two endings, written side by side, so no one can claim they were not told.{/idea}
now: You read two paths in a single breath, one bright and one dark. {idea}You are still standing at the fork.{/idea} Every ordinary choice today is a step toward one of them.
old: Hell is about other, really bad people.
new: Both endings are real, and my own deeds are walking me toward one.
try: Leave one sin today that you know you have been holding on to.

title: They enter it on the Day of Recompense.
subtitle: The Day when deeds are paid back
then: Ibn Kathir explains the Day of ad-Din as {idea}the Day of Reckoning, Recompense, and Judgement.{/idea} The same word appeared in verse 9: {trap}you deny ad-Din.{/trap} Those who denied that Day meet it.
now: You say maliki yawm ad-din in every rakah, often on autopilot. {idea}This is that Day.{/idea} Next time, slow down on those words.
old: Payback for what I do is a vague, distant idea.
new: There is a Day set for recompense, and I name it in every prayer.
try: In your next prayer, pause on maliki yawm ad-din and think of its meaning.

title: No absence from it, not even an hour.
subtitle: No break, no way out
then: Ibn Kathir explains {trap}they will not be absent for even one hour from the torment{/trap}, with no rest and no lightening. {idea}The verse is said while doors are still open{/idea}, to people who could still turn.
now: You get a final notice on a bill and still have a week to pay. {idea}This is that week.{/idea} The verse is serious so that you use the time you have, not so you despair.
old: There will always be another chance to fix things.
new: The chances are now. Allah warns me so I use them.
try: Ask Allah's forgiveness 100 times today, in any free moments.

title: Do you even know what that Day is?
subtitle: A question that magnifies
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}this is a magnification of the affair of the Day of Judgement.{/idea} After describing both destinations, Allah pauses to ask: {reward}what will make you know what it is?{/reward}
now: You hear a talk about the Day and think: yes, I know all this. {idea}The verse says you do not, not really.{/idea} Some truths need to be felt again, not just known.
old: I already know everything there is about the Day of Judgement.
new: The Day is bigger than anything I have pictured.
try: Sit quietly for two minutes today and honestly imagine standing before Allah.

title: Again: do you know what that Day is?
subtitle: The question asked twice
then: Ibn Kathir notes {idea}Allah affirms it by saying again{/idea} the same question, and then {reward}explains it{/reward} in the next verse. The repetition holds the listener still before the answer comes.
now: Your parent says your name twice when something really matters. You look up from your phone. {idea}This is that second calling of your name.{/idea}
old: Hearing the same reminder twice is just repetition.
new: When Allah repeats a question, He wants me to stop and listen.
try: Read verses 17 and 18 aloud slowly, and pause before reading 19.

title: No soul can help another. The command is Allah's.
subtitle: The answer to the question
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}no one will be able to benefit anyone else{/trap}, unless Allah permits. The Prophet ﷺ told his own clan: save yourselves from the Fire. Qatadah said, {idea}the Decision is Allah's today, but on that Day no one will dispute Him.{/idea}
now: You count on your parents' prayers, your sheikh's dua, your family's good name. {idea}Those are blessings, but you will stand alone.{/idea} The command is Allah's now too, so turn to Him now.
old: Someone good in my family will be able to help me then.
new: Only Allah decides that Day, and He already decides today, so I turn to Him now.
try: Make one dua today directly to Allah, without asking anyone else to pray for you first.
